transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Um, student health sent me here. They said my weight is too low and they can’t clear me for the youth workshops unless I get checked out. The number has been going down, I guess, but to me it kind of just feels like what happens when I’m really focused and busy.
Have you been avoiding eating certain foods or restricting your food intake because you’re worried about gaining weight or because of how you perceive your body?

Yeah. I mean, I do restrict what I eat. I kind of plan my day around not really eating—like coffee before studio, and maybe a few bites of something from the café if people are around and it would look weird not to.

I avoid bread and anything oily. It feels like if I eat that stuff, it’ll undo the control I’ve been working really hard to keep.
Have you been intentionally doing anything else to prevent weight gain, like excessive exercise, purging, or using laxatives?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I try to keep moving and I don’t like sitting around too much, but I don’t know if I’d call it excessive. I’m not doing anything like… I’m not sure what counts, I guess.
Can you describe what you mean by 'trying to keep moving'—do you feel driven to exercise even when you’re tired or not in the mood, or does it interfere with your daily activities?

I guess I mean I just don’t like being still for too long. I’ll walk instead of taking the bus sometimes, or pace around when I’m studying.

I don’t know if I’d say I feel “driven,” exactly. It’s more like I get uncomfortable if I’ve been sitting a lot. I’m not sure it really interferes with things… I still go to class and studio. I just try to keep active when I can.
Do you feel like your weight or body shape has more impact on how you see yourself than other people might realize?

Yeah… probably more than I like to admit. Like, when I look at photos from a showcase, I don’t really notice the artwork first. I immediately look at my arms or my waist.

If I look small enough, I feel more… serious, I guess. More put-together. And if I don’t, it kind of changes how I feel about myself.
Do you have a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if others might see you as underweight?

Yes. I do. Even the idea of gaining, like, one pound can make me panic. If I eat a normal dinner, or something with butter in it, I start thinking everyone will be able to tell, like I’ve lost control or lost my discipline.
Do you feel that your concerns about your weight or body shape are something others wouldn’t fully understand, even if they tried to put themselves in your shoes?

Yeah, I think so. I don’t think people really get how automatic it is for me. Like with showcase photos, I don’t even look at the artwork first—I go straight to my arms or my waist.

And if I look small enough, I feel like I’m… doing okay, like I seem serious and put-together. I know that probably doesn’t make sense to other people, but that’s where my mind goes.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, like missing periods or them stopping altogether?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping close track of it, so I don’t want to say something definite. I haven’t really noticed enough to know.
Have you missed your period for at least three consecutive months or has it stopped altogether?
I’m not sure. I don’t track it closely enough to say it’s been three months in a row, and I haven’t really noticed it stopping altogether.
Have you intentionally lost weight, or has the weight loss happened without you actively trying?

It’s been intentional. I plan most of my day around not really eating—like I’ll have coffee before studio, and maybe a few bites of something from the café if people are watching. I avoid bread or anything oily because it feels like it would undo the control I’ve worked for.
Have you noticed that your menstrual periods have stopped completely for at least three months?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t been tracking it, so I can’t say for sure that it’s been completely stopped for three months.
Have you had a complete absence of menstrual periods for at least three consecutive months?
I can’t say for sure. I haven’t kept track closely enough to know if it’s been three months straight with no period.
Have you had a complete absence of menstrual periods for at least three consecutive months?
I’m really not sure. I know you’re asking if it’s been three months in a row, but I haven’t been keeping track well enough to say yes to that.
Have you had a complete absence of menstrual periods for at least three consecutive months?
I really can’t confirm that. I know I haven’t been paying close enough attention to my cycle to say it’s been completely absent for three straight months.
Have you had a complete absence of menstrual periods for at least three consecutive months?
I don’t know for certain. I haven’t been tracking it closely enough to say it’s been totally absent for three months in a row.
Have you had a complete absence of menstrual periods for at least three consecutive months?
I’m sorry, I really don’t know. I haven’t kept track closely enough to say whether it’s been a full three months with nothing.
Have you noticed that your menstrual periods have completely stopped for at least three months in a row?
I can’t really say that I’ve noticed that clearly. I haven’t been keeping track well enough to know if it’s been three months in a row.
Can you tell me approximately what you currently weigh and how tall you are?

I’m not totally sure of the exact number today. Student health weighed me and said it’s too low for them to clear me for the youth workshops, and they said it’s kept dropping. I’m about the same height I’ve been, but I don’t have the exact measurement with me. To me it just feels like what happens when I’m busy and really focused.
